title: The Coming Asteroids Mining, the Future Global Equity

tasks: Task 1: Build a model measuring global equity across countries
Task 2: Model asteroid mining and its effect on equity
Task 3: Explore how changes in mining affect equity
Task 4: Measures to make the mining industry advance equity

section_map.summary: Four-task abstract: equity assessment, mining model, two changes, eight policies
Background, literature review in three parts, our work
Capability approach, 25 indicators, entropy weights, CV
GE matrix, mining chain, oligopoly, 2011UW-158 case

contributions.summary: Equity defined through Sen's capability approach, split into asset, achievement and group differences.
Coefficient of variation as the single inequity statistic, checked against 2000 and a World Bank report.
One named asteroid, 2011UW-158, priced at about 27 billion dollars.
Correlation screen at 0.3 before multiple regression.

dependency_graph.handoff: Equity scores and their coefficient of variation are recomputed after the mining shock

assumptions.summary: Mining is technically feasible and financially worth it.
Only a few countries can mine, which justifies the oligopoly.
Private companies mine; governments may invest.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 25 indicators, 205 countries, Our World in Data and World Bank. Benefit and cost normalization.

models.summary: GEA: entropy-weighted three-level index, equity as coefficient of variation.
AMG: GE matrix, mining chain, Cournot oligopoly, regression transmission.

verification.summary: Historical check: asset CV 1.2437 in 2000, 1.5332 in 2020, consistent with World Bank 2020.
Gaussian noise: sigma up to 0.8 keeps weight error below 5 percent.

results_trace.summary: Gender development index 0.721, below 0.8. Peace index 0.708473.
After one mission: asset CV 1.5332 to 1.5379, achievement CV 0.6912 to 0.6945.
More countries entering lowers the asset CV to 1.5359.

writing_logic.summary: Abstract is one paragraph per task, each opening 'For task N'.
Individual welfare stands in for national welfare, stated as 'in other words' plus 'vice versa'.
Three market characteristics listed, then 'we can think that this is an oligopoly market'.
Policy in three blocks, each tied back to one model result.

language_observations.summary: 'becomes an issue that must be studied' — necessity claimed in the second sentence.
Before-and-after numbers given to four decimals: 1.5332 to 1.5379.
Definition set off as its own line: 'provision of varying levels of support...'.
'Most countries still have a long way to go' — idiomatic close to a statistic.
'This also verifies the credibility of our model' — external report used as confirmation.
'we can think that this is an oligopoly market' — hedged classification after three premises.
Strengths labeled with single adjectives: Comprehensive, Objective, Credible, Robust.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Grounding equity in Sen's capability approach gives the index a theoretical ancestor.
Pricing one real asteroid is more convincing than a generic scenario.
Gaussian noise with a stated tolerance is a cleaner robustness test than shifting one parameter.

weaknesses.summary: Country treated as a whole, so individual welfare is approximated.
No real mining practice, so the model is idealized.
Political environment and the space economy are not quantified.

independent_extensions.summary: Report confidence intervals on the CV change, which is in the fourth decimal.
Quantify the geopolitical and environmental impacts instead of listing them.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Dispersion statistic as the equity measure, validated against an external report.

unresolved_questions.question: Where do the demand parameters a and b come from?
Is a CV change of 0.0047 distinguishable from noise?
